title: Kaleidofin -- about us
passage: Kaleidofin aims to provide fair and transparent financial solutions for millions of customers and enterprises in India lacking convenient access to formal financial services, focusing on the informal sector. The platform helps customers Save, Borrow, Protect, Retain and nurture through goal-based financial planning. Kaleidofin operates through Lending as a Service (co-lending, direct assignment, securitisation, business correspondent lending), Credit Assessment (ki score, ki view) and Customer Engagement, partnering with banks, banking correspondents, MFIs and NBFCs.

title: Kaleidofin Capital Secures $5 Million Debt Facility from Women's Livelihood Bond
passage: Kaleidofin Capital Private Ltd (KCPL) has secured a $5 million (approximately Rs 47.77 crore) debt facility through non-convertible debentures from WLB Asset VIIB Pte. Ltd., a special purpose vehicle established by Impact Investment Exchange (IIX), Singapore. The four-year debenture carries a globally recognised 'Orange Bond' certification. The proceeds will be deployed across the clean energy and financial inclusion sectors.

title: Kaleidofin: Fintech platform for the women, by the women
passage: Sucharita Mukherjee (co-founder and CEO) and Puneet Gupta founded Kaleidofin in 2017. The platform serves over 3 million users, of which 97 percent are women; approximately one million customers operate small businesses. Kaleidofin operates across 17 states through 50 channel partners. Products include Ki Score (AI/ML credit scoring), Ki Credit (onboarding/fraud middleware), Ki View (risk dashboard) and Ki Cash (digital savings and engagement).

title: Kaleidofin closes KES 276 million agri-finance securitisation in Kenya
passage: Kaleidofin closed a KES 276 million (approximately USD 2.1 million) securitisation backed by smallholder farmer input loans originated by Apollo Agriculture, covering 23,839 farmers (51% women borrowers, ~22% first-time borrowers). The transaction carries a BBB- investment-grade rating from Agusto and was supported by the IDH Farmfit Fund, FSD Africa, the UK's MOBILIST programme and British International Investment. The programme could eventually mobilise ~KES 2.37 billion and reach over 130,000 farmers.
